headline: OpenAI's pricing page appears to list an unannounced life-sciences model, gpt-rosalind-discovery, at the same price as its research version, TestingCatalog reports.
score_reason: Kept at pool 5: a real price-list entry, but OpenAI has announced nothing and the model's purpose is a guess.
importance_line: Researchers and drug-discovery teams that use GPT-Rosalind might get a second model for early-stage work, but OpenAI has said nothing, so the model's purpose, release date and access rules are unknown.
summary: TestingCatalog reports that OpenAI's API pricing page now lists gpt-rosalind-discovery, a variant of GPT-Rosalind (OpenAI's AI model for biology and drug research, open only to eligible organisations), beside gpt-rosalind-research at the same prices: $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens (tokens are small pieces of text). OpenAI has published no blog post or system card, so what the model does is unknown; TestingCatalog guesses from the name that it is aimed at drug discovery, but says that is only a guess.
notes: Read TestingCatalog in full. TestingCatalog credits the AI Tracker Bot on X for the first sighting. We did not check OpenAI's pricing page.
